narrative:
The model estimates a 51% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. Because of this, the company has decided not to offer you the promotion at this time.

The decision is driven mainly by three aspects of your profile. First, your overall work experience of 1–5 years pulled the prediction strongly toward staying; people with this relatively short total experience are much more likely to remain with their employer than those with longer careers. However, two other factors pushed harder in the opposite direction. The fact that you have received other job offers while working here increased the likelihood of leaving, as external opportunities often signal that someone is actively considering a move. Similarly, having spent only 1–5 years in your current role also nudged the prediction toward departure, since shorter tenure in the present organization is commonly associated with higher turnover.

Taken together, the pull from your external opportunities and limited time in this specific job outweighed the stabilizing effect of your modest overall experience, tipping the model just past the 50% mark.

The organization should consider discussing your career goals with you openly and exploring whether additional support, clearer advancement paths, or retention incentives could shift your outlook. You, in turn, may want to reflect on what would make staying feel more secure and fulfilling. Understanding these drivers can help both sides address the underlying concerns before the next promotion cycle.
